contradictions.topic: The tab that groups expense types under a tax authority is written 'Expense Types Group' and 'Expense Type Groups' inside one and the same topic, and only 'Expense Type Groups' in three others.

readings.summary: The process overview names the tab 'Expense Type Groups' (plural Groups) inside the full Administration menu path.
readings.sourceQuote: Administration > Invoice > Tax Administration > Expense Type Groups tab

readings.summary: The step-by-step procedure that actually drives the tab names it 'Expense Types Group' (plural Types, singular Group).
readings.sourceQuote: On the Expense Types Group tab, select from the Tax Authority list.

readings.summary: The very topic that wrote 'Expense Types Group' in its first numbered step writes 'Expense Type Groups' later in its own Applies To note - so the drift is inside a single topic, not only between topics.
readings.sourceQuote: The Applies To setting also appears as a column on the Expense Type Groups page.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe the Tax Administration tab strip for 'Expense Type Groups' FIRST - that is the form four separate files use - and accept 'Expense Types Group' only as a fallback if the primary probe finds nothing. The two are not coequal candidates, so do not 'take whichever resolves first'. A normalised match on the tokens expense/type/group (case-insensitive, tolerant of where the plural s falls) is the safe locator; never hard-match one literal string and fail. Record the literal text seen so later steps reuse the observed string rather than a guessed one.
contradictions.notes: Corpus weight: 'Expense Type Groups' occurs in four files (apply-vat-to-expense-type-groups-0efbc573, step-5-optional-add-a-new-expense-type-group-to-a-tax-authority-e8d87361, step-6-optional-add-a-new-vendor-group-to-a-tax-authority-d8b7786d, the-basic-process-12a5686d) while 'Expense Types Group' occurs in exactly one (e8d87361). Hypothesis: the singular-Group form is a transcription slip in a single numbered step. The alternative explanation - that the tab was renamed between releases and only one topic was updated - is ruled out by the corpus itself, because e8d87361 carries BOTH spellings, so the two forms demonstrably coexisted in one document at one time.

contradictions.topic: The left-menu entry that opens this tool is called the 'Tax Administration link' in some topics and the 'Tax Administrator link' in another.

readings.summary: The role-assignment step says the assigned user gains the 'Tax Administration link'.
readings.sourceQuote: Assign this role so that the user can see and work with the Tax Administration link.

readings.summary: The Tax Validation configuration step says the same user accesses the 'Tax Administrator link', which then displays the Tax Administration tool - so link and tool carry different names in the same sentence.
readings.sourceQuote: this user may now access the Tax Administrator link, which displays the Tax Administration tool.

readings.summary: The Tax Validation process overview describes SAP Concur staff exposing the 'Tax Administration link' in Invoice Admin.
readings.sourceQuote: exposing the Tax Administration link in Invoice Admin.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe the left menu for 'Tax Administration' FIRST; only if that finds nothing, retry with 'Tax Administrator'. Do not treat them as coequal candidates and do not click 'whichever is present' as if the order did not matter. Assert on the page that opens (the Tax Administration page with its tab strip), never on the link's exact word, and do not fail the run because the link reads 'Tax Administrator'.
contradictions.notes: Corpus weight: 'Tax Administrator link' occurs exactly once corpus-wide - step-3-configure-the-service-14c3ef13.md, line 23 - while 'Tax Administration link' occurs in two separate topics (step-2-assign-the-tax-administrator-role-b7f391c8.md and the-basic-process-13c136d5.md), a 2:1 split. The lone occurrence also self-corrects inside its own sentence, naming the destination 'the Tax Administration tool', which is why 'Tax Administrator' is recorded as the fallback rather than as a coequal name. Hypothesis: it is a writer's slip carried over from the role name (Invoice Tax Administrator) rather than a second real menu entry - but the corpus never states that, and a site could legitimately render either, so both are kept.

contradictions.topic: The role is written 'Invoice Tax Administrator' wherever a topic quotes the Available Roles list, and plain 'Tax Administrator' in prose, in step titles and in the required-roles topic.

readings.summary: The assignment procedure says the string to pick in the Available Roles list is 'Invoice Tax Administrator'.
readings.sourceQuote: Under Available Roles, select Invoice Tax Administrator, then click Add.

readings.summary: The required-roles topic states the prerequisite as the plain 'Tax Administrator' role.
readings.sourceQuote: To add and manage tax authorities, the user needs to have the Tax Administrator role.

readings.summary: The SAP-Concur-staff enablement step also uses the long form, saying the feature exposes the 'Invoice Tax Administrator' role in User Permissions.
readings.sourceQuote: expose the Invoice Tax Administrator role in User Permissions

readings.summary: The Tax Authority process overview uses the short form throughout, assigning 'the Tax Administrator role' in User Permissions.
readings.sourceQuote: The Tax Administrator role is assigned to an employee by using options in User Permissions

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Select the literal 'Invoice Tax Administrator' entry in User Permissions > Invoice > Available Roles: that is the only form used by any topic that actually quotes the list. Never search the list for an entry reading exactly 'Tax Administrator', and never fail a prerequisite check because a topic named the short form - match the list entry by CONTAINS 'Tax Administrator' and prefer the longest match. Assert success on the Tax Administration entry becoming reachable after Save, not on the role string.
contradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW. The corpus arguably shows the short form is shorthand rather than a competing list entry: both Step 2 topics are titled with the short form yet instruct selecting the long one from Available Roles (b7f391c8 'Under Available Roles, select Invoice Tax Administrator, then click Add.', and b903b7c8 line 33 'In the Available Roles list, select Invoice Tax Administrator, and then click Add.'), and no topic anywhere claims the list contains a literal entry 'Tax Administrator'. This node is therefore NOT a claim that two roles exist. It is kept, in the narrowed form above, because an automation that took the required-roles topic's short form as the list string would hunt for an entry that no topic evidences. Hypothesis: the short form is prose shorthand for the long one.

contradictions.topic: Three different navigation paths are given for reaching User Permissions to assign the Invoice Tax Administrator role.

readings.summary: One Step 2 topic gives a single collapsed path starting at User Administration and describes it as part of the Company Admin tool.
readings.sourceQuote: Click User Administration > User Permissions > Invoice tab of the Company Admin tool.

readings.summary: The other Step 2 topic (same title, different loio) starts at Administration > Company > Company Admin and then treats User Permissions as a left-menu item.
readings.sourceQuote:
1.  Click Administration > Company > Company Admin.
    
2.  Click User Permissions (left menu) and then click the Invoice tab.

readings.summary: The enablement topic gives a third, shorter path: User Admin > User Permissions.
readings.sourceQuote: the Concur User Admin role can now assign it to a user via User Admin > User Permissions.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not encode a fixed click path to User Permissions. Drive to the User Permissions screen by trying, in order, the top menu entries 'Administration > Company > Company Admin', 'User Administration', and 'User Admin', then look for a 'User Permissions' left-menu item; treat arrival at a screen that offers an Invoice tab plus an Available Roles list as the success condition.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the menu tree differs by provisioning and by which admin roles the signed-in user holds (a user with only User Admin may see a different top-level entry than one with full Company Admin), so all three paths may be simultaneously correct on different tenants.

contradictions.topic: The tax-provider client identifier appears as a Field-column label, 'Partner Account Number', in the configuration topic and only as an activity name, 'Entering the Unique Tax Partner Number', in the page-options topic.

readings.summary: The Tax Validation configuration topic prints 'Partner Account Number' as the Field-column label of the first option on the Tax Validation page, with the description of the provider-issued account number beside it.
readings.sourceQuote:
Partner Account Number
    

 | 

This is the unique account number provided by a tax service provider to the client.

readings.summary: The Tax Validation page options topic calls the same identifier the 'Unique Tax Partner Number' and gives the same meaning - the number the provider issues to identify the client.
readings.sourceQuote: Entering the Unique Tax Partner Number: The tax service provider issues unique numbers to each of their clients so that they can identify the client.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: On the Tax Validation tab, resolve this input by the Field-column label 'Partner Account Number' - the only form any topic presents as a label - and enter the provider-issued account number there. Do NOT wait for, or require, a control labelled 'Unique Tax Partner Number'; if the screen shows only that string, fill it and record the observed label. There is exactly one input here: the Tax Administration roster carries both strings as separate field records (taxValidationPartnerAccountNumber and uniqueTaxPartnerNumber), so fill one and never treat the second as a second input to complete. FOR THE ROSTER OWNER: uniqueTaxPartnerNumber is probably a phantom field derived from prose and should be reviewed.
contradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW. The two topics may simply be naming the field and the value it holds rather than disagreeing: 14c3ef13 gives the label with the description 'This is the unique account number provided by a tax service provider to the client', which is what c3fe1df5's activity name describes typing. Hypothesis for that reading: c3fe1df5's list is a series of gerund activity names ('Entering...', 'Deciding...', 'Mapping...', 'Activating...'), and the one bullet in that list which does name a control quotes the control exactly ('the feature is activated by selecting (enabling) the Turn On Tax Validation check box'), which suggests the rest are prose rather than labels. The record is kept in narrowed form because an automation told to expect a 'Unique Tax Partner Number' control would look for a label the configuration topic never prints. Source-character note: the label is printed in that topic's field table as a bullet, '-   Partner Account Number'; the quote begins after the bullet marker so a bare grep -F does not read it as a command-line option. Merge provenance: the raw Group 5B data recorded all three of these labels as ONE record ('Tax Validation option labels', found twice - by the tax crosscut lens and the tax tables lens). The duplicate pair was collapsed, and the surviving record was then SPLIT into three nodes, one per control, because each control resolves to its own field and so can carry its own appliesTo; a single node could not.

Hypothesis, same as the sibling records: c3fe1df5's bullets are gerund step names rather than labels - the one bullet in that list which does name a control uses the control's exact string ('the Turn On Tax Validation check box'). Kept in narrowed form only so that an automation does not hunt for a 'Request Type to be Analyzed' label the configuration topic never prints. Merge provenance: the raw Group 5B data recorded all three of these labels as ONE record ('Tax Validation option labels', found twice - by the tax crosscut lens and the tax tables lens). contradictions.topic: After predefining a tax code, one topic says four tax code fields become lists and its twin says only VAT Tax Code 1 does.

readings.summary: The gerund-titled topic says predefining a code turns the tax code fields 1 through 4 into lists on the invoice.
readings.sourceQuote: The user will now see the tax code fields (1-4) as a list in the Invoice Details and Itemization Summary sections of the invoice.

readings.summary: The Step 7 twin of the same procedure says only the single VAT Tax Code 1 field becomes a list.
readings.sourceQuote: The user will now see the VAT Tax Code 1 field as a list in the Invoice Details and Itemization Summary sections of the invoice.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: The Tax Code tab action itself is identical under both readings - create the code and Save - so perform it once. Do NOT assert how many downstream fields turned into lists: verify by inspecting the invoice form afterwards and report the observed count (1 or up to 4), and never fail the step because only VAT Tax Code 1 became a list.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the count is provisioning-dependent - a site that has only added VAT Tax Code 1 in Forms and Fields would see one list, while a site with all four added would see four - which would make both topics true on different tenants. The corpus never says this.

contradictions.topic: The first hop to the Tax Administration page is 'Invoice' in some topics and 'Invoice Admin' in another.

readings.summary: The Tax Validation configuration topic routes through 'Invoice Admin' instead of 'Invoice'.
readings.sourceQuote: As the Invoice Tax Administrator, click Administration > Invoice Admin > Tax Administration. The Tax Administration page appears.

readings.summary: The Access Tax Authorities topic routes the first hop through 'Administration > Invoice' and then clicks Tax Administration in the left menu.
readings.sourceQuote:
1.  Click Administration > Invoice.
    
2.  Click Tax Administration left menu. The Tax Administration page appears.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Navigate in two moves, not one: open the Administration menu and click whichever of 'Invoice' or 'Invoice Admin' exists, then click 'Tax Administration' in the left menu. Treat the appearance of the Tax Administration page (its tab strip) as the success assertion; do not encode a single dotted path string.
contradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW from four readings to the one hop that genuinely differs. The other two paths are not competing accounts and are recorded here instead: 'Select Administration > Invoice > Tax Administration (left menu).' (configure-predefined-tax-codes-6b42509f.md) and 'Click Administration > Invoice > Tax Administration (left menu).' (step-7-optional-configure-predefined-tax-codes-be8bc5b8.md) are the SAME path differing only in the verb - most likely a republication artefact of gerund vs imperative topic titles rather than two different gestures - and 2fae4ae3 writes that same path as two numbered steps, which is a rendering difference, not a disagreement. Hypothesis: 'Invoice Admin' and 'Invoice' are two renderings of the same top menu entry, differing by release or by which Invoice modules the site has provisioned. Cross-reference (NOT merged): the Company Locations navigation node records the same 'Invoice' vs 'Invoice Admin' alias on the way to a different destination page. The two were kept separate because they are disagreements about two different navigation targets, and an automation resolves them at different moments; the shared alias is noted so a fix to the menu-resolution strategy is applied to both.

contradictions.topic: Whether the US, Canada and India are supported for VAT in Concur Invoice - the admin guide excludes exactly the countries the tools guides give VAT field implementations for.

readings.summary: The admin guide states outright that the US, Canada, India and other multi-tax countries are NOT supported for VAT.
readings.sourceQuote: Countries that are not supported for VAT in Concur Invoice are the US, Canada, India, and other multi-tax countries.

readings.summary: The tools guide gives Canada two complete VAT implementation options - four dedicated VAT fields or two - with province-specific labelling.
readings.sourceQuote: There are different ways to implement VAT for a client in Canada. The following section describes how to implement four and two VAT tax fields respectively.

readings.summary: The tools guide also gives the US a VAT field assignment alongside the UK, Japan and Australia.
readings.sourceQuote: For the UK, the US, Japan, and Australia, use the VAT Amount 1 field, which is for primary tax.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Never gate a configuration run on a country allow-list derived from the admin guide. If asked to configure VAT for a US, Canadian or Indian entity, proceed with the field-level configuration the tools guides describe, and surface the admin guide's unsupported-countries statement to the human as an open question rather than refusing or silently skipping.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: 'supported' means different things in the two guides - the admin guide is describing Tax Authority automatic VAT calculation (which needs a single tax per authority, so multi-tax countries fall out), while the tools guides describe Capture Processing field capture, which merely reads printed tax amounts into VAT Amount fields. The corpus never states this distinction, so both readings stand. Merge provenance: this same disagreement was raised independently by the tax crosscut lens and the tax tables lens over the identical three files; the two records were collapsed into this one node. appliesTo is deliberately empty - the disagreement is about product-level country support, not about any control on the Tax Administration page.

contradictions.topic: The two twin OCR/Capture 'fields supported for capture' tables enumerate Canadian tax capture differently - one carries Canada in Vat 1 plus a Vat 2 row, the other has neither.

readings.summary: The tools guide's table names Canada GST/HST inside the Vat 1 primary-tax cell.
readings.sourceQuote: Vat 1 (Primary Tax - Canada GST/HST, Australia GST, US Tax, VAT UK/Japan) **

readings.summary: The same tools table adds a separate Vat 2 secondary-tax cell for Canada PST/QST at header level.
readings.sourceQuote: Vat 2 (Secondary Tax – Canada PST/QST) *

readings.summary: The admin guide's twin of the same table drops Canada from the Vat 1 cell entirely and has no Vat 2 row at all.
readings.sourceQuote: Vat 1 (Australia GST, US Tax, VAT UK/Japan) *

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: When adding capture fields, enumerate what the Add Fields dialog actually offers instead of asserting either table's row set; add Vat 2 only if it is present, and do not treat its absence as a failure. This pair belongs to the Capture Processing form configuration, not to Tax Administration, so no Tax Administration field is claimed from it.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the tools guide's table is the newer of the two twins (it adds Canada and a Vat 2 row, and its footnote markers differ - ** vs *), so the admin guide may simply be a stale republication. The corpus gives no dates to settle it.

contradictions.topic: How many VAT amount fields are available - the Tax Authority feature is said to support only one, while the form-field inventories document four.

readings.summary: The Add VAT Fields step states flatly that Tax Authority currently supports only one VAT amount field, naming the trio VAT Amount 1 / VAT Rate 1 / VAT Tax Code 1.
readings.sourceQuote: Currently, in Tax Authority, Concur Invoice only supports one VAT amount field (VAT Amount 1/VAT Rate 1/VAT Tax Code 1).

readings.summary: The tools guide instructs Canadian clients to implement four dedicated VAT tax fields.
readings.sourceQuote: can implement four dedicated VAT Tax fields for this purpose.

readings.summary: The admin guide's own available-fields table documents four VAT amount fields and says some countries will have all four.
readings.sourceQuote: Some countries will have four VAT amount fields because clients have more than one type of tax assessed, and all the VAT amounts need to be stored.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Add whichever VAT fields the Forms and Fields Add Fields dialog offers - up to four - but when configuring Tax Authority rates and groups, only assume VAT Amount 1 participates in automatic calculation. Treat VAT Amount 2 to 4 as capture/extract carriers until a run proves otherwise, and never fail because Tax Authority ignores fields 2 to 4.
contradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW. The 'only one' sentence carries its own scope in its quoted words - 'Currently, in Tax Authority, ...' - and neither competing reading enters that scope: canada-de22c9f9.md is about implementing form fields for capture and never mentions Tax Authority, and available-vat-fields-8b395ce2.md opens 'The following fields are available when working with VAT at the header and line item level', an inventory of available form fields. The two counts may therefore be compatible, one narrower than the other. The record is kept because the boundary decides how many fields an automation should expect to matter on the Tax Authority page, and no topic says what becomes of VAT Amount 2-4 there. Hypothesis: the 'only one' statement scopes to Tax Authority's automatic VAT calculation while the four-field guidance scopes to form fields and Capture Processing extraction - which the same Canada topic hints at by saying VAT Amount 3 and 4 must be entered manually. The corpus never draws that boundary explicitly beyond the three words 'in Tax Authority'.

contradictions.topic: The Applies To document type is written 'Payment Request' in the expense type group wizard and 'Payment request' in the vendor group wizard.

readings.summary: The expense type group wizard capitalises both words of the document type.
readings.sourceQuote: Select the Payment Request document type for which to calculate VAT for expense type groups.

readings.summary: The vendor group wizard lowercases 'request' for what is otherwise the same Applies To value.
readings.sourceQuote: Select the Payment request document type for which to calculate VAT for vendor groups.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Prefer the capitalised 'Payment Request' when selecting the Applies To value - corpus-wide it is the form in 135 files against 2 for 'Payment request' - and match case-insensitively so either rendering resolves. Never compare the option string byte-for-byte across the two wizards and never fail a step on the casing alone. Applies to both expenseTypeGroupAppliesTo and vendorGroupAppliesTo, which is why this attaches to no single field.
contradictions.notes: NARROWED AFTER REVIEW to a probable typo rather than two option values. Hypothesis: a shift key missed while copying one wizard topic from the other - the two sentences are otherwise word-for-word twins differing only in the trailing noun ('for expense type groups' / 'for vendor groups'), and corpus-wide 'Payment Request' appears in 135 files while 'Payment request' appears in 2 (this vendor-group topic and process-overview-payment-request-import-8b42995f.md). CORRECTION to the raw record's note: the sentence 'The Applies To setting also appears as a column on the Expense Type Groups page.' is NOT peculiar to the vendor-group topic - it sits at line 96 of BOTH wizard topics, which is itself evidence of copying. It has no competing reading, so it is recorded here rather than as its own node.

contradictions.topic: State/Province is optional on the Company Locations add-address form but mandatory in the Purchase Order address import records that create the same rows

readings.summary: The Company Locations add-address field table marks State/Province as optional, so an address typed on the page can be saved with the state or province left blank.
readings.sourceQuote:
State/Province
    
    (Optional)

readings.summary: The Company Locations topic's own revision history records State/Province being changed TO optional on September 9, 2016, confirming the optional marking is deliberate and dated rather than a table typo. (Source characters: in the file this bullet is written '-   State/Province field now an optional field' with a leading hyphen and three spaces; the quote drops the leading '-   ' so that a bare grep -F does not read it as a command-line option.)
readings.sourceQuote: State/Province field now an optional field

readings.summary: The Purchase Order Bill-to Address (record type 210) import format marks State/Province Required? = Y, so a bill-to address arriving by import must carry a state or province.
readings.sourceQuote:
State/Province

 | 

Maximum 255 characters

 | 

Y

readings.summary: The Purchase Order Ship-to Address (record type 220) import format likewise marks State/Province Required? = Y for the ship-to twin of the same address record.
readings.sourceQuote:
State/Province

 | 

Maximum 255 characters

 | 

Y

readings.summary: The linkage the disagreement depends on, stated by the add-address topic itself: the Address Code typed on the Company Locations form is identical to the External ID field of the Purchase Order Bill To and Ship To record sets - so the page and the 210/220 import are two entry paths onto the same address records rather than unrelated stores. This reading takes no side; it establishes that the two sides collide.
readings.sourceQuote: This value is identical to the External ID field used in the Bill To and Ship To record sets of the Purchase Order import.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat State/Province as OPTIONAL when driving the Add New Ship To / Bill To Location window - do not fail a step because the field is blank, and do not assert a required-field error if it is left empty. Treat it as REQUIRED when generating or validating a Purchase Order 210/220 import row: always populate it there. If a single value set feeds both paths, populate State/Province unconditionally, because that satisfies both accounts; never assert the reverse (that a blank one will be rejected on screen).
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the two rules belong to two different entry paths rather than to one stored constraint - the browser form relaxed the rule in 2016 while the batch importer's record specification was never re-cut, so the same logical address column is validated differently depending on whether it arrives through the UI or the feed file. A second, weaker hypothesis is that the import requirement is a file-format (positional column) requirement rather than a value requirement, but the corpus never says so.

contradictions.topic: Name is required on the Company Locations add-address form but optional in the Purchase Order address import records

readings.summary: The Company Locations add-address field table marks Name as required - and elsewhere in the same table Name is the value searched on when picking a Bill To or Ship To address.
readings.sourceQuote:
Name
    
    (Required)

readings.summary: The Purchase Order Bill-to Address (record type 210) import format calls Name an optional name, so a bill-to address can be imported with no Name at all.
readings.sourceQuote: An optional name that can be used to identify a particular address.

readings.summary: The Purchase Order Ship-to Address (record type 220) import format says the same for the ship-to twin - the name is optional and merely 'can be given' to the address.
readings.sourceQuote: An optional name that can be given to the address.

readings.summary: The linkage the disagreement depends on, stated by the add-address topic itself: the Address Code typed on the Company Locations form is identical to the External ID field of the Purchase Order Bill To and Ship To record sets - so the page and the 210/220 import are two entry paths onto the same address records rather than unrelated stores. This reading takes no side; it establishes that the two sides collide.
readings.sourceQuote: This value is identical to the External ID field used in the Bill To and Ship To record sets of the Purchase Order import.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Always write a Name when creating an address through the UI - the form will block Save without one. When reading existing rows back (including rows that arrived through the PO import), do NOT assume every Company Locations row has a Name: a nameless row is legal by the import spec, and any automation that locates an address by typing its Name into a Bill To / Ship To picker will silently fail to find it. Locate such rows by Address Code / External ID instead.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: the UI requirement is a form-level validation added for searchability (the same table says the system searches for the location by Name), while the importer keeps Name optional for backward compatibility with feed files keyed on External ID. Stated as a hypothesis - the corpus never reconciles the two.

readings.summary: The Bill-to Address (record type 210) import format defines Country Code as exactly 2 characters - a fixed width, not a ceiling.
readings.sourceQuote:
Country Code

 | 

2 characters

readings.summary: The Ship-to Address (record type 220) import format defines the same column as a maximum of 2 characters, which would also admit a 1-character value.
readings.sourceQuote:
Country Code

 |
